summary: Transactional outbox command seam appended to backbone write plans before live broker publisher integration.
claim_boundary: Transactional outbox write seam only. This slice persists protocol dispatch metadata as parameterized SQL commands inside the same tenant-scoped SqlExecutionPlan as business rows. It does not implement a live outbox poller, broker publisher, gRPC server, retry worker, dead-letter processor, or exactly-once delivery proof.

facets.F1_simplicity: A small shared kernel appends one static service-specific outbox insert command to existing write batches instead of introducing a broker SDK or runtime worker dependency.
facets.F2_hyperscaler: Backbone write plans now preserve business-row and protocol-dispatch intent in one tenant-scoped transaction plan, reducing the future live publisher's coupling to REST/app handlers.
facets.F3_adversarial: Tests cover outbox command ordering after business statements, tenant/envelope scope-drift refusal, service-specific SQL selection, REST/app command-count updates, and migration distribution/RLS validation.
facets.F5_quality: Focused outbox/app/adapter tests plus the 36-package backbone check/test/clippy/fmt matrix, cargo-deny, license-policy, dependency-seam, honest-claims, workflow/catalog parsing, Jenkins parsing, and diff hygiene are part of this run.
facets.F7_security_privacy: Outbox commands use SQL parameters for tenant, audit, policy, idempotency, AsyncAPI, and proto metadata and do not persist payload bodies or raw message/mail/post content.
facets.F11_observability: The outbox table captures dispatch_state, attempt_count, audit_correlation_id, policy_decision_ref, event_kind, aggregate_id, AsyncAPI metadata, and proto metadata for future publisher telemetry correlation.
